nodes.label: ABSURD
nodes.doc: A name NOTHING in this tree provides: if either directive below goes quiet, `this` has degraded to `any` and every other result in this file is vacuous.

nodes.label: bare
nodes.doc: A directive over a line with no error is TS2578, which is what makes this file fail loudly when a check is relaxed.

nodes.label: CARD
nodes.doc: The wire a page annotates, and not the exonode read straight out of the package.

nodes.label: dom
nodes.doc: Structural rather than imported: this package maps `@exodra/core` and not `@exodra/dom`.

nodes.label: FILLS_ONE_PORT
nodes.doc: THE CONTROL: without it the directives above pass equally well if `render` refused EVERYTHING.

nodes.label: HIGHLIGHT_PACK
nodes.doc: A PACK THE WAY AN APPLICATION WRITES ONE: one name, one factory, and the factory ignores `next` because nothing shipped owns this name.

nodes.label: HIGHLIGHTS
nodes.doc: Spelled BY HAND: an unannotated `(c) => …` has no inference site and lands on `unknown`, which satisfies every negative directive below while nothing is checked.

nodes.label: hydrating
nodes.doc: Packs composed the other way round: the name still resolves, the prototype being the backend.

nodes.label: narrowed
nodes.doc: `TExoPort` is the WIDE type, so it does not go back into a holder declared for one kind.

nodes.label: NESTS_HIGHLIGHTS
nodes.doc: `c.one`, `c.list` and `c.build` take components too, so the refusal must hold from INSIDE one.

nodes.label: notATable
nodes.doc: The table is a branded token with a `unique symbol` key: nothing outside a backend produces one.

nodes.label: notAttr
nodes.doc: And the four refusals that make the four lines above mean something.

nodes.label: portable
nodes.doc: The portable surfaces core publishes, which were narrow before this change and stay narrow.

nodes.label: ROW
nodes.doc: BARE `TExoDomNode`: naming the highlight half would DEMAND the pack, and a row wanting less than the receiver has still goes in.
